summary: Prefix catalog resync delay leads to repeated prompt latency and occasional client-side timeouts
description:
Issue summary: Customers report higher-than-expected latency and intermittent client-side timeouts when sending repeated short prompts (followup turns) to pinned model endpoints. Impact: Degraded P99 latency for repeat prompts; several customer requests timed out and were retried by clients. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated pool for PromptlyAI. Observed on redwood-open-3B and redwood-llama-7B. Steps to reproduce:
1) Create a short-turn conversation (single-turn prompt) and call the API repeatedly with identical prompt payloads at ~20 qps.
2) Observe response latency distribution and streaming disconnects.
3) Reproduce against the customer's pinned endpoint (dedicated) and generic hosted endpoint for same model.
Observed behavior: P95/P99 latency for repeat prompts jumps from baseline ~120ms to 800ms-2s in bursts; some requests return 504 client-side after stream disconnect. Logs show a resync cycle for the prefix catalog and a burst of KV cache cold-path reads immediately after. Expected behavior: Repeat identical prompts should hit warm prefix/KV cache and return within baseline latency with streaming intact. Additional context: Customer only started seeing regression after the weekly catalog resync job deployed 2026-03-10. The customer is on a production SLA and reported business impact (in-app search degradation).

2026-03-12 16:10 - Support - Ava Martinez: Notified customer of findings and provided short-term workaround (route repeat-turn traffic to fallback model variant on other pool). Customer accepted workaround to mitigate user impact while we fix root cause.
investigation_notes: Trace IDs: rQh7-20260311-01 (p99 latency 1.8s), rQh7-20260311-02 (stream disconnect at 1.2s).

Observability: 'kv.resync.duration' spikes coincident with 'serving.request.fallback.count' increases. Dashboard indicates resync job runs every 24h, the recent run duration increased from ~80ms to ~600ms after change in PR #2148.

Hypothesis: Recent change (PR #2148) to prefix-catalog resync introduces a global catalog lock while updating shard mappings; this causes in-memory index to be briefly unavailable and requests hit cold-path backfill (per-key KV lease acquisition) leading to serialized latency on hot keys for repeated prompts.
Repro run: Synthetic traffic test at 25 qps on dedicated pool reproduced p99 latency spike when resync triggered. Disabling the resync job on one staging pool removed spike immediately.
Related logs: kvcache-service stderr snippet (2026-03-11T09:28Z): 'WARN prefix_catalog: lock_acquire_time=612ms, shard_reindex=true, fallback_to_backfill=true'
resolution: Workaround applied: Traffic routing rule created in Console to send PromptlyAI repeat-turns to alternate pool (pool-3) for 48 hours to avoid resync window. Hotfix plan: revert the global-locking change from PR #2148 and reintroduce incremental shard update with per-shard locks. Engineering will ship patch (kvcache v1.4.7) and deploy to prod-us-east during a low-traffic window. Post-deploy validation: run synthetic 25 qps repeat prompt test and monitor kv.resync.duration and serving.request.fallback.count for 48h. Follow-ups: (1) Add telemetry alarm if resync duration >250ms, (2) Update runbook with safer resync strategy, (3) Coordinate with PromptlyAI on a scheduled maintenance window for final rollout. Target ETA for full fix: 2026-03-18.
